name: User
rationale: Represents ordinary authenticated users and the common supertype for application actors.
plain_english_summary: A person who can log in to iTrust.
source_excerpt: ordinary authenticated User

name: User__mid
rationale: MID is the user authentication identifier and is assigned to some users.
plain_english_summary: The user's medical identification number used for login and identification.
source_excerpt: A user authenticates with MID and password.
alternatives_considered: Modeled as a Credential attribute, but the spec treats MID as a user identifier.

name: User__password
rationale: Password is required for authentication and credential-secrecy policies.
plain_english_summary: The user's password credential.
source_excerpt: A user authenticates with MID and password.
alternatives_considered: Modeled as a separate Credential resource, but direct user attribute is sufficient for secrecy and authentication requirements.

name: User__securityQuestion
rationale: Security question access is specifically prohibited for HCPs.
plain_english_summary: The security question associated with the user's account.
source_excerpt: The HCP must not enter, edit, or view the patient's security question or password.
alternatives_considered: Modeled as a Credential attribute, but the requirement names it as patient account data.

name: Patient
rationale: Represents patients as principals and as selected patient resources.
plain_english_summary: A patient whose health information is stored in iTrust.
source_excerpt: Important actors include Patient, HCP, LHCP, DLHCP, Administrator, Emergency Responder, UAP, Personal Representative, Public Health Agent, Lab Technician, Software Tester, and ordinary authenticated User.

name: Patient__isActive
rationale: Deactivated patients cannot be modified or log in and may be reactivated only by administrators.
plain_english_summary: Whether the patient account is currently active.
source_excerpt: A deactivated patient cannot be modified or log into the system and can only be reactivated by an administrator.
alternatives_considered: Used deactivated as a Bool, but positive isActive better supports normal access checks.

name: Hcp
rationale: Represents health-care professionals who create, edit, and view patient information.
plain_english_summary: A health-care professional using iTrust.
source_excerpt: Doctors and other health-care workers can obtain and share essential patient information and view aggregate patient data.

name: Lhcp
rationale: Represents licensed health-care professionals with patient-designation semantics.
plain_english_summary: A licensed health-care professional, such as a provider who can be designated by a patient.
source_excerpt: Important actors include Patient, HCP, LHCP, DLHCP, Administrator, Emergency Responder, UAP, Personal Representative, Public Health Agent, Lab Technician, Software Tester, and ordinary authenticated User.

name: Lhcp__hospitals
rationale: Administrators assign LHCPs to multiple hospitals from the hospital list.
plain_english_summary: The hospitals where the licensed health-care professional is assigned.
source_excerpt: An administrator can assign an LHCP to multiple hospitals, choosing only hospitals from the hospital list.
alternatives_considered: Modeled assignment as a separate resource, but a set attribute directly captures the stated multiple hospitals.

name: Administrator
rationale: Represents administrators who manage accounts, credentials, and deactivated patients.
plain_english_summary: An administrative user who manages users and system settings.
source_excerpt: Important actors include Patient, HCP, LHCP, DLHCP, Administrator, Emergency Responder, UAP, Personal Representative, Public Health Agent, Lab Technician, Software Tester, and ordinary authenticated User.

name: EmergencyResponder
rationale: Represents emergency responder users created by administrators.
plain_english_summary: A user who responds to emergencies in the healthcare system.
source_excerpt: An administrator can create LHCPs, emergency responders, lab technicians, and public health agents.

name: Uap
rationale: Represents unlicensed personnel who can be created by LHCPs and access medical data.
plain_english_summary: An unlicensed assistant or personnel user in iTrust.
source_excerpt: A LHCP can create UAP users.

name: PersonalRepresentative
rationale: Represents users acting as patient-specific representatives.
plain_english_summary: A person authorized to act for a particular patient.
source_excerpt: Personal representative status is also patient-specific.

name: PublicHealthAgent
rationale: Represents public health agent users created by administrators.
plain_english_summary: A public health agent user in iTrust.
source_excerpt: An administrator can create LHCPs, emergency responders, lab technicians, and public health agents.

name: LabTechnician
rationale: Represents lab technician users created by administrators.
plain_english_summary: A lab technician user in iTrust.
source_excerpt: An administrator can create LHCPs, emergency responders, lab technicians, and public health agents.

name: SoftwareTester
rationale: Represents software tester actors listed in the requirements slice.
plain_english_summary: A software tester account in iTrust.
source_excerpt: Important actors include Patient, HCP, LHCP, DLHCP, Administrator, Emergency Responder, UAP, Personal Representative, Public Health Agent, Lab Technician, Software Tester, and ordinary authenticated User.

name: Hospital
rationale: Represents hospitals from the hospital list used for LHCP assignments and office visits.
plain_english_summary: A hospital known to iTrust.
source_excerpt: An administrator can assign an LHCP to multiple hospitals, choosing only hospitals from the hospital list.

name: Session
rationale: Represents authenticated sessions for login and timeout authorization checks.
plain_english_summary: A user's logged-in session in the application.
source_excerpt: Authenticated sessions terminate after inactivity, logout, or closing the application.

name: Session__user
rationale: Sessions are authenticated for a particular user.
plain_english_summary: The user who owns the session.
source_excerpt: A user authenticates with MID and password.
alternatives_considered: Used action context only, but session ownership is a stable relationship.

name: Session__isActive
rationale: Authorization is disabled after session inactivity termination conditions.
plain_english_summary: Whether the session is currently active.
source_excerpt: After the inactivity limit is exceeded, authorization is disabled.
alternatives_considered: Stored only last activity time, but the access rule needs active/inactive state directly.

name: SystemSettings
rationale: Represents administrator-configurable system settings such as inactivity period length.
plain_english_summary: Global configuration for the iTrust application.
source_excerpt: The administrator can set the inactivity period length.

name: SystemSettings__inactivityPeriodLength
rationale: The inactivity period length is configurable by administrators.
plain_english_summary: How long a session may be inactive before authorization is disabled.
source_excerpt: The administrator can set the inactivity period length.

name: MedicalRecord
rationale: Represents patient medical records as protected resources.
plain_english_summary: A patient's medical record in iTrust.
source_excerpt: Important resources include patient accounts, credentials, demographic information, medical records, diagnostic information, office visits, access logs, provider designations, personal-representative relationships, and authenticated sessions.

name: MedicalRecord__patient
rationale: Own-record and represented-record permissions require the target patient identity.
plain_english_summary: The patient whose record this is.
source_excerpt: for their own records and for patients they represent
alternatives_considered: Used context.patient, but the record itself is owned by a patient.

name: DemographicInformation
rationale: Represents demographic information that UAPs can enter and edit.
plain_english_summary: Demographic details about a patient.
source_excerpt: UAP can enter and edit demographic information, diagnosis, office visit notes, and other medical information, and can view records.

name: DemographicInformation__patient
rationale: Demographic information belongs to a selected patient.
plain_english_summary: The patient whose demographic information this is.
source_excerpt: The HCP can enter a patient as a new user and can edit the patient according to the patient data format, but the patient MID cannot be edited.

name: DiagnosticInformation
rationale: Represents diagnostic information with patient-controlled viewing restrictions.
plain_english_summary: A diagnosis or diagnostic detail about a patient.
source_excerpt: Approved diagnostic information is diagnostic information that a patient allows a designated or other licensed health-care professional to view.

name: DiagnosticInformation__patient
rationale: Diagnostic information access is controlled by the patient it concerns.
plain_english_summary: The patient whose diagnostic information this is.
source_excerpt: Approved diagnostic information is diagnostic information that a patient allows a designated or other licensed health-care professional to view.

name: DiagnosticInformation__isRestricted
rationale: Selected diagnoses can have restricted viewing.
plain_english_summary: Whether viewing this diagnosis has been restricted by the patient.
source_excerpt: For selected diagnostic information, such as mental-illness, substance-abuse, or cosmetic surgery diagnoses, the patient can restrict viewing.
alternatives_considered: Used a diagnosis category enum, but the access decision only requires whether it is restricted.

name: DiagnosticInformation__restrictionAllowed
rationale: An LHCP determines whether the patient may restrict viewing of a diagnosis.
plain_english_summary: Whether this diagnosis may be restricted by the patient.
source_excerpt: A licensed health-care professional determines whether the patient is allowed to restrict viewing of a diagnosis.
alternatives_considered: Modeled as context for restrict action, but it is a persistent determination about the diagnosis.

name: DiagnosticInformation__allowedAudience
rationale: Restricted diagnostic information can be viewable by designated LHCPs, other LHCPs, or no one.
plain_english_summary: Which group the patient permits to view restricted diagnostic information.
source_excerpt: A patient can enable designated licensed health-care professionals, other licensed health-care professionals, or no one to view restricted diagnostic information.
alternatives_considered: Used an enum entity, but a simple string keeps the atom set smaller unless the reviewer wants enumerated audience values.

name: OfficeVisit
rationale: Represents office visits that HCPs document and patients view or survey.
plain_english_summary: A documented visit between a patient and healthcare provider.
source_excerpt: An HCP can document and edit office visits for a selected patient, including date, hospital, notes, prescriptions, lab procedures, diagnoses, procedures, immunizations, and referrals.

name: OfficeVisit__patient
rationale: Office visits are for selected patients and support own/represented access checks.
plain_english_summary: The patient who had the office visit.
source_excerpt: An HCP can document and edit office visits for a selected patient, including date, hospital, notes, prescriptions, lab procedures, diagnoses, procedures, immunizations, and referrals.

name: OfficeVisit__lhcp
rationale: Patients can view LHCPs they have ever had an office visit with.
plain_english_summary: The licensed healthcare professional associated with the visit.
source_excerpt: A patient can view all LHCPs the patient has ever had an office visit with and all LHCPs the patient has designated.
alternatives_considered: Used Hcp type, but the requirement specifically refers to LHCPs visited.

name: OfficeVisit__hospital
rationale: Office visit documentation includes the hospital.
plain_english_summary: The hospital where the office visit occurred.
source_excerpt: including date, hospital, notes, prescriptions, lab procedures, diagnoses, procedures, immunizations, and referrals

name: OfficeVisit__surveyTaken
rationale: Survey access depends on whether the office-visit satisfaction survey has already been taken.
plain_english_summary: Whether the satisfaction survey for this office visit has already been submitted.
source_excerpt: If a patient or personal representative has not taken an office-visit satisfaction survey, they may take the survey; after the survey has been taken, they cannot take or view the previously submitted survey through that path.
alternatives_considered: Modeled survey as separate resource, but the requirement ties the state to the office-visit path.

name: PersonalHealthInformation
rationale: Represents personal health information viewable by patients and representatives and editable by HCPs.
plain_english_summary: Personal health details in a patient's health record.
source_excerpt: A patient or personal representative can view medical records, family history, personal health information, immunizations, and office-visit information for their own records and for patients they represent.

name: PersonalHealthInformation__patient
rationale: Own and represented access requires linking personal health information to a patient.
plain_english_summary: The patient whose personal health information this is.
source_excerpt: for their own records and for patients they represent

name: FamilyHistory
rationale: Represents family history as a protected part of patient records.
plain_english_summary: Family medical history for a patient.
source_excerpt: A patient or personal representative can view medical records, family history, personal health information, immunizations, and office-visit information for their own records and for patients they represent.

name: FamilyHistory__patient
rationale: Family history access is scoped to own or represented patients.
plain_english_summary: The patient whose family history this is.
source_excerpt: for their own records and for patients they represent

name: Immunization
rationale: Represents immunizations as patient record data viewed and edited in office visits.
plain_english_summary: A patient's immunization information.
source_excerpt: personal health information, immunizations, and office-visit information

name: Immunization__patient
rationale: Immunization records are accessed for own or represented patients.
plain_english_summary: The patient whose immunization record this is.
source_excerpt: for their own records and for patients they represent

name: AccessLog
rationale: Represents access logs that patients may view for themselves or represented people.
plain_english_summary: A record of who accessed a patient's information and when.
source_excerpt: Access logs include accessor name, accessor role relative to the patient, date/time, and transaction type.

name: AccessLog__patient
rationale: Viewing access logs depends on the patient whose log it is.
plain_english_summary: The patient whose access log this entry belongs to.
source_excerpt: A patient can view their own access log, or the access log for a person for whom they are a personal representative.

name: AccessLog__accessorName
rationale: Access logs include the accessor name.
plain_english_summary: The name of the person who accessed the information.
source_excerpt: Access logs include accessor name, accessor role relative to the patient, date/time, and transaction type.
alternatives_considered: Used accessor entity, but the requirement specifically lists accessor name.

name: AccessLog__accessorRoleRelativeToPatient
rationale: Access logs include the accessor role relative to the patient.
plain_english_summary: How the accessor is related to the patient for this access event.
source_excerpt: Access logs include accessor name, accessor role relative to the patient, date/time, and transaction type.

name: AccessLog__dateTime
rationale: Access logs include the date and time of the transaction.
plain_english_summary: When the access happened.
source_excerpt: Access logs include accessor name, accessor role relative to the patient, date/time, and transaction type.

name: AccessLog__transactionType
rationale: Access logs include the transaction type.
plain_english_summary: What kind of access or transaction occurred.
source_excerpt: Access logs include accessor name, accessor role relative to the patient, date/time, and transaction type.

name: ProviderDesignation
rationale: Represents patient-specific DLHCP designations rather than a flattened global role.
plain_english_summary: A relationship showing that a patient designated a licensed provider.
source_excerpt: DLHCP is not just a global principal type; it is a licensed professional designated by a particular patient.

name: ProviderDesignation__patient
rationale: Designated provider status is specific to a patient.
plain_english_summary: The patient who made the designation.
source_excerpt: DLHCP is not just a global principal type; it is a licensed professional designated by a particular patient.
alternatives_considered: Made DLHCP a global entity only, but the review focus requires patient-specific relationships.

name: ProviderDesignation__lhcp
rationale: The designated provider is an LHCP selected by the patient.
plain_english_summary: The licensed healthcare professional designated by the patient.
source_excerpt: A patient can designate or undesignate any LHCP as a DLHCP for that patient.

name: ProviderDesignation__isDesignated
rationale: Designation and undesignation require current designation state.
plain_english_summary: Whether the LHCP is currently designated for the patient.
source_excerpt: A patient can designate or undesignate any LHCP as a DLHCP for that patient.
alternatives_considered: Deleted designation resources on undesignation, but a Bool preserves relationship history if needed.

name: PersonalRepresentativeRelationship
rationale: Represents patient-specific personal representative relationships.
plain_english_summary: A relationship showing that one user represents a particular patient.
source_excerpt: Personal representative status is also patient-specific.

name: PersonalRepresentativeRelationship__patient
rationale: Representative status is scoped to a particular patient.
plain_english_summary: The patient being represented.
source_excerpt: A patient can view their own access log, or the access log for a person for whom they are a personal representative.

name: PersonalRepresentativeRelationship__representative
rationale: The relationship must identify the user who may act as representative.
plain_english_summary: The user who represents the patient.
source_excerpt: An HCP can add or remove another registered user as a personal health representative for a selected patient.
alternatives_considered: Used PersonalRepresentative entity only, but the requirement says another registered user can be added for a selected patient.

name: PersonalRepresentativeRelationship__isActive
rationale: Add and remove actions require current relationship state.
plain_english_summary: Whether the representative relationship is currently active.
source_excerpt: An HCP can add or remove another registered user as a personal health representative for a selected patient.
alternatives_considered: Deleted relationship resources on removal, but a Bool supports explicit removal state.

name: login
rationale: Users authenticate with MID and password against a session-like resource.
plain_english_summary: Log in to iTrust.
source_excerpt: A user authenticates with MID and password.

name: logout
rationale: Sessions terminate on logout.
plain_english_summary: Log out of iTrust.
source_excerpt: Authenticated sessions terminate after inactivity, logout, or closing the application.

name: requestPasswordChange
rationale: Users may request password changes.
plain_english_summary: Ask to change one's password.
source_excerpt: The user may request a password change.

name: setInactivityPeriodLength
rationale: Administrators configure the inactivity timeout setting.
plain_english_summary: Set how long inactive sessions remain authorized.
source_excerpt: The administrator can set the inactivity period length.

name: createPatient
rationale: HCPs can create patient accounts.
plain_english_summary: Create a new patient account.
source_excerpt: An HCP can create or disable a selected patient.

name: disablePatient
rationale: HCPs can disable selected patients.
plain_english_summary: Deactivate a selected patient account.
source_excerpt: An HCP can create or disable a selected patient.

name: reactivatePatient
rationale: Administrators are the only actors identified for patient reactivation.
plain_english_summary: Reactivate a deactivated patient account.
source_excerpt: A deactivated patient cannot be modified or log into the system and can only be reactivated by an administrator.

name: editPatient
rationale: HCPs can edit patient data but not MID, security question, or password.
plain_english_summary: Edit a selected patient's account data.
source_excerpt: The HCP can enter a patient as a new user and can edit the patient according to the patient data format, but the patient MID cannot be edited.

name: createLhcp
rationale: Administrators can create LHCP users.
plain_english_summary: Create a licensed health-care professional user.
source_excerpt: An administrator can create LHCPs, emergency responders, lab technicians, and public health agents.

name: createEmergencyResponder
rationale: Administrators can create emergency responder users.
plain_english_summary: Create an emergency responder user.
source_excerpt: An administrator can create LHCPs, emergency responders, lab technicians, and public health agents.

name: createLabTechnician
rationale: Administrators can create lab technician users.
plain_english_summary: Create a lab technician user.
source_excerpt: An administrator can create LHCPs, emergency responders, lab technicians, and public health agents.

name: createPublicHealthAgent
rationale: Administrators can create public health agent users.
plain_english_summary: Create a public health agent user.
source_excerpt: An administrator can create LHCPs, emergency responders, lab technicians, and public health agents.

name: createUap
rationale: LHCPs can create UAP users.
plain_english_summary: Create an unlicensed assistant personnel user.
source_excerpt: A LHCP can create UAP users.

name: assignLhcpCredentials
rationale: Administrators assign medical identification numbers and passwords to LHCPs.
plain_english_summary: Assign an MID and password to an LHCP.
source_excerpt: An administrator can assign medical identification numbers and passwords to LHCPs.

name: assignLhcpHospital
rationale: Administrators assign LHCPs to hospitals from the hospital list.
plain_english_summary: Assign a licensed healthcare professional to a hospital.
source_excerpt: An administrator can assign an LHCP to multiple hospitals, choosing only hospitals from the hospital list.

hospital.name: assignLhcpHospital__context__hospital
hospital.rationale: The chosen hospital must be represented for the assignment action.
hospital.plain_english_summary: The hospital being assigned to the LHCP.
hospital.source_excerpt: An administrator can assign an LHCP to multiple hospitals, choosing only hospitals from the hospital list.

name: viewLhcps
rationale: Patients can view LHCPs they visited or designated.
plain_english_summary: View licensed healthcare professionals associated with the patient.
source_excerpt: A patient can view all LHCPs the patient has ever had an office visit with and all LHCPs the patient has designated.

patient.name: viewLhcps__context__patient
patient.rationale: The patient whose visited or designated LHCP list is being viewed must be explicit.
patient.plain_english_summary: The patient whose provider list is being viewed.
patient.source_excerpt: A patient can view all LHCPs the patient has ever had an office visit with and all LHCPs the patient has designated.

name: addProvider
rationale: Patients can add LHCPs to their provider list.
plain_english_summary: Add a licensed provider to the patient's provider list.
source_excerpt: A patient can add a LHCP to the patient provider list.

name: designateLhcp
rationale: Patients can designate LHCPs as patient-specific DLHCPs.
plain_english_summary: Mark an LHCP as designated for a patient.
source_excerpt: A patient can designate or undesignate any LHCP as a DLHCP for that patient.

name: undesignateLhcp
rationale: Patients can remove patient-specific DLHCP designation.
plain_english_summary: Remove an LHCP's designated-provider status for a patient.
source_excerpt: A patient can designate or undesignate any LHCP as a DLHCP for that patient.

name: viewAccessLog
rationale: Patients can view their own access log or one for a represented patient.
plain_english_summary: View a patient's access log.
source_excerpt: A patient can view their own access log, or the access log for a person for whom they are a personal representative.

name: viewMedicalRecord
rationale: Patients and personal representatives can view medical records for their own or represented records.
plain_english_summary: View a patient's medical record.
source_excerpt: A patient or personal representative can view medical records, family history, personal health information, immunizations, and office-visit information for their own records and for patients they represent.

name: viewFamilyHistory
rationale: Patients and representatives can view family history for own or represented patients.
plain_english_summary: View family medical history.
source_excerpt: A patient or personal representative can view medical records, family history, personal health information, immunizations, and office-visit information for their own records and for patients they represent.

name: viewPersonalHealthInformation
rationale: Patients and representatives can view personal health information for own or represented records.
plain_english_summary: View personal health information.
source_excerpt: A patient or personal representative can view medical records, family history, personal health information, immunizations, and office-visit information for their own records and for patients they represent.

name: viewImmunization
rationale: Patients and representatives can view immunizations for own or represented records.
plain_english_summary: View immunization information.
source_excerpt: A patient or personal representative can view medical records, family history, personal health information, immunizations, and office-visit information for their own records and for patients they represent.

name: viewOfficeVisit
rationale: Patients and representatives can view office-visit information for own or represented records.
plain_english_summary: View office-visit information.
source_excerpt: A patient or personal representative can view medical records, family history, personal health information, immunizations, and office-visit information for their own records and for patients they represent.

name: takeOfficeVisitSurvey
rationale: Survey taking depends on whether the office-visit survey has already been taken.
plain_english_summary: Submit an office-visit satisfaction survey.
source_excerpt: If a patient or personal representative has not taken an office-visit satisfaction survey, they may take the survey; after the survey has been taken, they cannot take or view the previously submitted survey through that path.

name: viewDiagnosticInformation
rationale: Approved and restricted diagnostic information has special patient/LHCP viewing rules.
plain_english_summary: View diagnostic information about a patient.
source_excerpt: Approved diagnostic information is diagnostic information that a patient allows a designated or other licensed health-care professional to view.

name: restrictDiagnosticInformation
rationale: Patients can restrict viewing of selected diagnostic information.
plain_english_summary: Restrict who may view a diagnosis.
source_excerpt: A patient can restrict viewing on selected diagnostic information.

name: determineDiagnosisRestrictionAllowed
rationale: LHCPs determine whether a patient may restrict viewing of a diagnosis.
plain_english_summary: Decide whether a diagnosis can be restricted by the patient.
source_excerpt: A licensed health-care professional determines whether the patient is allowed to restrict viewing of a diagnosis.

name: editPersonalHealthInformation
rationale: HCPs can enter and edit selected patients' personal health records.
plain_english_summary: Enter or edit a patient's personal health information.
source_excerpt: An HCP can enter and edit a patient's personal health records.

name: editImmunization
rationale: HCPs can edit immunizations for selected patients.
plain_english_summary: Edit a patient's immunization information.
source_excerpt: An HCP can edit historical values, immunizations, office-visit information, family history, BMI, and death status for a selected patient.

name: editFamilyHistory
rationale: HCPs can edit family history for selected patients.
plain_english_summary: Edit a patient's family history.
source_excerpt: An HCP can edit historical values, immunizations, office-visit information, family history, BMI, and death status for a selected patient.

name: documentOfficeVisit
rationale: HCPs can document office visits for selected patients.
plain_english_summary: Create documentation for an office visit.
source_excerpt: An HCP can document and edit office visits for a selected patient, including date, hospital, notes, prescriptions, lab procedures, diagnoses, procedures, immunizations, and referrals.

name: editOfficeVisit
rationale: HCPs can edit office visits for selected patients.
plain_english_summary: Edit an office visit record.
source_excerpt: An HCP can document and edit office visits for a selected patient, including date, hospital, notes, prescriptions, lab procedures, diagnoses, procedures, immunizations, and referrals.

name: enterDemographicInformation
rationale: UAPs can enter demographic information.
plain_english_summary: Enter patient demographic information.
source_excerpt: UAP can enter and edit demographic information, diagnosis, office visit notes, and other medical information, and can view records.

name: editDemographicInformation
rationale: UAPs can edit demographic information.
plain_english_summary: Edit patient demographic information.
source_excerpt: UAP can enter and edit demographic information, diagnosis, office visit notes, and other medical information, and can view records.

name: addPersonalRepresentative
rationale: HCPs can add another registered user as a personal representative for a selected patient.
plain_english_summary: Add a personal representative for a patient.
source_excerpt: An HCP can add or remove another registered user as a personal health representative for a selected patient.

name: removePersonalRepresentative
rationale: HCPs can remove a personal representative for a selected patient.
plain_english_summary: Remove a personal representative from a patient.
source_excerpt: An HCP can add or remove another registered user as a personal health representative for a selected patient.
